lines.text: Now the timing maths. Every time is on one clock. Say now is twelve point five zero zero seconds.
The photo's age has three parts: zero point zero one five since it arrived, plus the camera's capture and processing time, eight and twelve thousandths.
Together, zero point zero three five seconds. So the photo was taken at twelve point four six five.
Ignore the age, and the error is v, the speed, times the age. One point five times zero point zero three five: about five centimeters.
The wheel memory stores a dot every four thousandths of a second. Our capture time falls between two dots.
At twelve point four six four, x was zero point nine nine eight five. At twelve point four six eight, it was one point zero zero four five.
Our moment is a quarter of the way from one to the other.
So x is zero point nine nine eight five, plus a quarter of six millimeters: exactly one. A straight line blend between the dots.
In our simulator, timing mistakes barely hurt a straight approach. Turning while looking at the tag is where they really matter.
